title: CSV full outer join
prompt: Build a CLI reading one JSON object {key,left,right} from stdin, where key is a column name and left and right are CSV texts. CSV rules: UTF-8 text; records end with LF or CRLF; fields may be double-quoted, in which case they may contain commas, line breaks and doubled quotes ("" means one quote); a double quote inside an unquoted field is an ordinary character; a closing quote must be followed by a comma, a line ending or the end of input, otherwise the input is not valid CSV; a leading byte order mark is ignored; completely empty lines are skipped; an unterminated quoted field makes the input invalid. Each side's first record is its header; header names must be unique within a side and both headers must contain key, otherwise (and for empty CSV texts, invalid CSV, or malformed input JSON) exit nonzero, leave stdout empty and write a diagnostic to stderr. A data record is rejected, and counted for its side, when its field count differs from its header's or its key field is empty. Perform a full outer join on exact string equality of the key field. Output columns: key first, then the left columns other than key in left order, then the right columns other than key in right order; a non-key name present in both headers is renamed left_NAME on the left side and right_NAME on the right side. Rows: for each distinct key present on either side, in plain code-unit string order of the key, emit one row for every combination of a left record and a right record with that key (left records in input order outermost, right records in input order inner); a key present on only one side emits that side's records with null for every column of the other side. Print exactly one JSON object and a newline: {columns,rows,rejected} where rows are arrays of cell strings or null aligned to columns, and rejected is {left,right} counts. Exit 0 on success. No external services are needed.
